diagram_math_checks.result: All three vertices are positive braid remainders: A₀=σ₁σ₂², A₁=σ₂, A₂=1. Arrows are algorithm steps removing a LEFT prefix, not morphisms or order edges. A₀=(σ₁σ₂)σ₂=a₁A₁ and A₁=σ₂·1=a₂A₂; the exact equations on the arrows fix the multiplication direction (step 4.1; normal-form supplier (b)).

Step 1.2 gives σ₁∧Lσ₂=1. Left multiplication by D=σ₁σ₂ gives Δ∧Lσ₁σ₂²=D, using Δ=Dσ₁ and A₀=Dσ₂ (step 2.1), so a₁ is the maximal simple prefix. Δ=σ₂(σ₁σ₂) makes a₂ left-divide Δ and hence Δ∧LA₁=a₂. Lengths 2 and 1 exclude both 1 and Δ, whose lengths are 0 and 3; both factors are proper simple (step 4.1). The same first gcd is exactly (a₁a₂)∧LΔ=a₁, the left-weighted condition (steps 3.2 and 5.1).

Using Δ=σ₁σ₂σ₁, Δ⁻¹σ₁σ₂=σ₁⁻¹ after adjacent inverse cancellations. Thus x=σ₁⁻¹σ₂=Δ⁻¹(σ₁σ₂)σ₂ with Δ power on the LEFT (step 1.1). The computed gcd has length 2<3, so Δ does not left-divide A₀. The unique pair criterion of F7 then gives p(x)=−1 (step 3.1), which also excludes positivity by F7.

Existing verification is byte-for-byte intact and proves every displayed equation independently. The figure asserts exactly two directed remainder transitions and no lattice, braid crossings, or permutation cycle conventions.
